chain.label: Certification compliance shown only by engineering drawing review
chain.trigger: compliance with the applicable certification regulation (14 CFR 25.679) for the G-IV was demonstrated by a review of engineering drawings

chain.label: Gust lock/throttle interlock allowed 3-4 times the intended 6 degree throttle lever angle
chain.trigger: postaccident testing on nine in-service G-IV airplanes found that, with the gust lock handle in the ON position, the forward throttle lever movement that could be achieved on the G-IV was 3 to 4 times greater than the intended TLA of 6 degrees

caused_by.evidence: There was no functional test of the design of the G-IV gust lock/throttle interlock system. A drawing review was an insufficient means of demonstrating compliance with 14 CFR 25.679

chain.label: Habitual crew noncompliance with checklists and absence of standard callouts
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers did not routinely use the normal checklists or the optimal challenge-verification-response format

chain.label: Gust lock not disengaged at engine start and flight control check omitted
chain.trigger: the flight crew failed to disengage the gust lock system as called for in the Starting Engines checklist and failed to conduct a flight control check as called for in the After Starting Engines checklist

caused_by.evidence: lack of adherence to industry best practices involving the execution of normal checklists eliminated the opportunity for them to recognize that the gust lock handle was in the ON position and delayed their detection of this error

chain.label: Elevators, ailerons, and rudder locked by the engaged gust lock
chain.trigger: The FDR recorded restricted motion of both the elevator and rudder throughout the taxi and attempted takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the restricted motion is consistent with the flight crew failing to disengage the gust lock system as called for in the Starting Engines checklist

chain.label: Night lighting made the red gust lock handle less conspicuous
chain.trigger: the accident occurred at night in lower lighting conditions, when the color red is less conspicuous and would, therefore, be less easily noticed by either pilot

chain.label: Nonfrangible approach lights and localizer antenna along the extended centerline, with a ravine beyond the perimeter fence
chain.trigger: the airplane collided with structures that were not mounted on frangible supports... came to rest spanning a ravine formed by the Shawsheen River

chain.label: Crew never noticed the ON gust lock handle or the yoke failing to move to neutral by 80 kt
chain.trigger: the flight crew did not notice that the gust lock handle was in the ON position during taxi, line up, or the initial portion of the takeoff roll

caused_by.evidence: they would likely not inspect the gust lock handle unless they were specifically checking its status, a step the accident flight crew did not perform during engine start
although the gust lock handle was painted red... the accident occurred at night in lower lighting conditions, when the color red is less conspicuous

chain.label: Throttle levers stopped by the interlock; EPR plateaued at 1.42 instead of the normal 1.7
chain.trigger: the engine pressure ratio (EPR) did not reach the expected level due to the throttles contacting the gust lock/throttle lever interlock

caused_by.evidence: When the gust lock handle is in the ON position, the throttles can move freely until the interlock is contacted and further forward travel is stopped
an interlock that limited TLA to 6 degrees would have prevented the airplane from achieving any significant acceleration, thus constituting an unmistakable warning

chain.label: PIC forced the throttles forward with the autothrottle instead of rejecting the takeoff
chain.trigger: The PIC did not immediately reject the takeoff; instead, he engaged the autothrottle, and the throttle levers moved slightly forward

caused_by.evidence: The PIC did not likely understand the reason for the throttle lever restriction and attempted to force the levers forward with the help of the autothrottle
the PIC did not immediately call out the problem or call for a rejected takeoff before engaging the autothrottle... an example of ineffective communication

chain.label: Gust lock handle lock pin fractured, letting the throttles advance to near-target EPR
chain.trigger: The most likely explanation for an increase of this magnitude is that the gust lock handle's lock pin failed at this time

caused_by.evidence: As a result of the autothrottle engagement, and possibly due, in part, to manual forces applied to the throttle levers, the lock pin in the gust lock handle was likely broken or compromised, allowing the throttle levers to move forward

chain.label: Pilot activated the FPSOV at 150 kt trying to release the gust lock, an ineffective strategy that also disabled the spoilers
chain.trigger: one of the pilots activated the FPSOV, likely in an attempt to unlock the flight controls, but this action was ineffective because high aerodynamic loads on the elevator were likely impeding gust lock hook release

caused_by.evidence: the delay in initiating a rejected takeoff likely resulted, in part, from surprise but also from a knowledge-based mistake stemming from an incomplete mental model of the gust lock system

chain.label: Rejected takeoff delayed about 10 seconds after the first 'lock is on' call, with power reduction 4 seconds later still
chain.trigger: the flight crew delayed applying brakes for about 10 seconds and further delayed reducing power by 4 seconds; therefore, the rejected takeoff was not initiated until the accident was unavoidable

caused_by.evidence: the PIC attempted to rotate the airplane, discovered that he could not move the control yoke, and began calling out '(steer) lock is on'
the delay in initiating a rejected takeoff was apparently exacerbated by the flight crew's attempt to use an ineffective strategy to resolve the problem and continue the takeoff
neither pilot verbally commanded a rejected takeoff... the absence of standard callouts diminished the flight crew's ability to develop a shared understanding of the situation
This increase in EPR may have contributed to the flight crewmembers' confusion about the nature of the problem and given them some confidence that they could continue the takeoff

chain.label: Airplane overran runway 11 at about 151 kt and crossed the paved overrun onto the grass
chain.trigger: the airplane exited the runway onto the paved overrun area at a groundspeed of about 151 kts

caused_by.evidence: if the flight crew had initiated a rejected takeoff at the time of the PIC's first 'lock is on' comment or at any time up until about 11 seconds after this comment, the airplane could have been stopped on the paved surface
the ground spoilers did not automatically deploy following the throttle reduction, which is consistent with the activation of the FPSOV

chain.label: Collision with approach lights, localizer antenna, and perimeter fence, coming to rest in the ravine
chain.trigger: the airplane collided with approach lights and a localizer antenna, passed through the airport's perimeter fence, and came to a stop in a ravine

caused_by.evidence: After leaving the paved runway overrun and entering the grass, the airplane collided with structures that were not mounted on frangible supports
all of the support structures that came in contact with the airplane were either broken or bent, and the airplane was likely substantially damaged as a result of contacting these structures

chain.label: Immediate postcrash fire; all seven occupants died of smoke inhalation and thermal injuries
chain.trigger: The two pilots, a flight attendant, and four passengers died. The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: the impact forces from the accident were survivable, but the cabin and cockpit environment quickly deteriorated due to the postcrash fire, which erupted immediately, spread rapidly, and prevented the occupants from escaping
the airplane was inside the ravine, which acted as a shield and kept the fire and heat centrally located and difficult to fight
